Results :

Scanning
Electron
Microscopy :
By
using
scanning
electron
microscopy
to
examine
the

dorsal
head
and
arm
region
of
the
cuttlefish ,
the
epidermal
head
lines
characterized
by

Budelmann
and
Bleckmann
( 1988 )
were
viewed .
Each
line
consisted
of
a
groove

containing
hair
cells
that
possessed
many
kinocilia
( up
to
12
μm
in
length ) .
The
hair
cells

did
not
form
a
continuous
line ;
single
hair
cells
and
groups
of
hair
cells
occurred
in

alternation
( Sundermann
1983 ) .

Although
a
range
of
frequencies
from
9
Hz

to
20,000

was
tested
( limited
by
the
capabilities
of
the
hydrophone ) ,
responses
were

only
observed
for
frequencies
between
9
and
9260
Hz .
All
responses
were
divided
into

two
categories ;
startle
and
non - startle
behavioral
responses .
Startle
responses
include
color

flashes ,
head
retractions ,
or
increasing
fin
beats
and

immediately
( within
3-8
video

frames )
at
the
onset
of
the
first
sound
pulse .

startle
behavioral
responses
are

distinguishable
from
startle
responses
in
that
the
reactions
are
more
prolonged ,
appear
to
be

controlled ,
and
are
not
subject
to
habituation .
